kurz: Yeast eats sugar from the flour and gives off gas and aromas. The gas puffs up the dough, the aromas make the flavour.
bild_im_kopf: Like millions of tiny air pumps that only work when they are warm enough and have something to eat.
was_passiert: Yeasts are living fungi. They turn sugar into carbon dioxide and alcohol and form aroma compounds along the way. They are most active between about 27 and 32 °C; in the fridge they work only very slowly. From about 55–60 °C they die, which is why the rise ends in the oven.
warum_wichtig: Temperature controls how fast the dough rises. Slow and cool gives more flavour, fast and warm gives more volume in a short time.
faustregeln: A cool, long prove for flavour; a warm, short one when it has to be quick.
Never put salt directly onto the yeast.
Fully proved: a finger dent fills back slowly, not immediately and not at all.
typische_fehler: Proving too warm for too long: the network tears and the dough collapses.

praxis.text: Prove overnight in the fridge: more aroma, a better crust, a more flexible schedule.
Braided loaves and enriched yeast cakes rise more slowly, because sugar and butter slow the yeast down.
